pr_title: [upnp] Fix url extension for JPEG_TN dlna_profile
pr_body:
## Description
This is quite an obscure use case but kodi can be used as the upnp renderer of its own upnp server/library. In such cases, kodi fails to display the artwork thumb in the video osd. This happens because even though the server thumb url is created by kodi and has the dlna_profile set to jpeg, the complete url has the extension of the media item (e.g. .flac, .mp3, etc). It works and downloads the image but kodi internal mechanisms to probe media (e.g. `GetMimeType()` won't flag the item as an image). Since we have full control of these server resources, just add `/thumb` to the url to avoid the possibility of flagging the image as audio/video.

## Motivation and context
Fix https://github.com/xbmc/xbmc/issues/20845

## How has this been tested?
Runtime tested, bubleupnp on android, kodi as renderer, kodi as upnp source.

## What is the effect on users?
0.0000001% of users will have thumbs when using a upnp client as remote for kodi internal music library :)

## Screenshots (if appropriate):
**Before:**
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/7375276/189396861-1aa9f88b-e389-4e40-a5ca-e7dce672b36d.png)


**Now:**
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/7375276/189396468-8735315e-4230-460b-a549-5d1eb71c8bd9.png)

pr_comments: Yeap it is kind of a workaround to the problem but at the same time it's logical that client applications might infer a given remote file is an audio file if it ends up as .mp3 or .flac avoiding (for example) expensive and slow head requests.
Shouldn't we also look into improving the client / renderer side to properly process the DLNA profile into a more accurate MIME type?

@Montellese imho I don't think so. The GetMimeType() method is used in a lot of places in Kodi. The likelihood of introducing regressions in other parts of the codebase (or making other parts slow) is quite high for the benefits that improvement can possibly bring. This issue doesn't only occur in Kodi - if you download one of the thumbs (extension .MP3 or .flac) your file browser will certainly associate it to a music player despite the fact the file is a picture. Behaviour could be different but at what performance cost?

@enen92 
"0.0000001% of users will have thumbs when using a upnp client as remote for kodi internal music library :)"

Not necessarily, in my development I can build playlists with various original files (DLNA, SMB, CLOUD, WEBDAV, FTP, internal...etc)
So it may concern 0.005% :))!

For me the workaraound is to point the url to an http server on the phone. (ex: http://lan_ip_of_phone:54467/art_downloaded_from_kodi_dlna_server.png)

## Bug report
### Describe the bug
Hello,
I am working on an android application which is able to drive UPNP / DLNA renderers.
I am using Cling, everything is ok with Kodi except two things:

1- I can't seem to get the baseUrl that allows me to get the KODI icon. Cling returns a null baseUrl to me. The uri returned for the icon is /icon256x256.png. For the other renderers I can get the bitmap with baseUrl + iconUri.

2- When I play a song in the KODI library to KODI, the album art url is not displayed. No problem if I play from another UPNP server.

Here is a clear and concise description of what the problem is:
<!--- Provide a more detailed introduction to the issue itself, and why you consider it to be a bug -->
<!--- A bug report that is not clear will be closed -->
<!--- Put your text below this line -->
1-  The baseURL returned by Cling  with:
````java
device.getDetails().getBaseURL()
````
is null for KODI.
The Uri of icon returned  is : /icon256x256.png 

2- For album art issue:
it seems that the problem is the same with other apps like bubleUpnp and HIFIcast ...
